claim: Large alternative managers are operating credit-routing platforms at institutional scale.
current_claim_grade: Level 4 official platform and deployment proof
strongest_current_evidence: Ares total AUM; Credit Group AUM; U.S. and European direct-lending AUM; Q2 and LTM direct-lending commitments and transaction counts; Apollo/Athene; KKR/Global Atlantic; Blackstone; Brookfield derived metrics.
what_this_proves: The platform-scale private-credit channel is real and measurable.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove borrower-level bank replacement or same-dollar source-to-use matching.
next_required_evidence: Repeat the same AUM, inflow, deployment, origination, and direct-lending mix metrics over multiple quarters and years.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not call platform AUM bank displacement.

claim: Private credit reaches named operating borrowers in real industries.
strongest_current_evidence: BDC schedule rows and transaction-role evidence for Valcourt, AeriTek, Sunvair, MAI, Relation, Frontline, Atwell, Precinmac, Jiffy, Auctane, and Medallia.
what_this_proves: Named borrowers and instruments can be tied to disclosed private-credit holders or arrangers.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove total facility size, all lender roles, or use of proceeds unless borrower documents exist.
next_required_evidence: Pull credit agreements, rating reports, UCC records, payoff notices, and borrower 8-Ks for each borrower case.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not equate visible fair value with total debt.

claim: Private credit can replace or repay specific bank-administered facilities.
current_claim_grade: Level 5 for isolated cases; Level 2 for broad claim
strongest_current_evidence: Auctane closing 8-K confirms termination of a prior bank-led credit agreement; Medallia has acquisition debt and repayment evidence; Atwell remains a live pursuit case.
what_this_proves: Specific borrower-level bank-facility takeout can be proven in some cases.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove banks are broadly disappearing from lending.
next_required_evidence: Build repeated borrower cases and compare lane-matched private-credit activity to bank C&I, syndicated, and leveraged-lending denominators.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not generalize isolated borrower takeouts into a market-wide claim.

claim: Insurance and retirement liabilities are a major capital source for credit and private-asset platforms.
strongest_current_evidence: Apollo/Athene invested assets and spread earnings; KKR/Global Atlantic credit AUM and insurance investments; Brookfield invested insurance assets and private-credit allocation; Blackstone insurer-client SMA inflows.
what_this_proves: Insurance-linked capital is visible as a real funding channel.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not show exact liability dollars funding named borrowers.
next_required_evidence: Pull NAIC/statutory Schedule D and Schedule BA, state filings, rating reports, and affiliated-investment details.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not say all insurer assets are private credit.

claim: Credit risk is moving into insurer-linked and private-credit channels.
strongest_current_evidence: KKR/Global Atlantic mortgage-loan past-due metric and FHLB pledged-assets metric; Brookfield and Apollo derived allocation metrics; current statutory/rating detail still missing.
what_this_proves: Some risk and funding-location clues are visible.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not establish full credit quality, capital adequacy, ratings migration, or loss risk.
next_required_evidence: Add statutory asset schedules, ratings mix, impairments, non-accruals, liquidity terms, RBC/capital ratios, and rating-agency overlays.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not infer safety or danger from scale alone.

claim: Data-center and electrification demand is moving from commentary into tariffs, service agreements, and customer obligations.
current_claim_grade: Level 4 for AEP Ohio and Duke ESAs; Level 3 broader lane
strongest_current_evidence: AEP Ohio data-center tariff effective date, PowerClerk/study/LOA/ESA mechanics, collateral, minimum-demand, exit-fee terms; Duke secured ESAs and pipeline; AEP signed and expected load bridge.
what_this_proves: Some load is crossing into legal and operational obligation processes.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove every requested GW is binding, approved, financed, or in service.
next_required_evidence: Extract final tariff orders, customer contract treatment, interconnection status, operating-company split, and quarter-by-quarter signed versus expected load definitions.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not add signed, expected, late-stage, and under-construction load buckets together.

claim: Utility capital plans are becoming regulatory and rate-base capital-flow claims.
current_claim_grade: Level 3 to Level 4 depending on jurisdiction
strongest_current_evidence: AEP and Duke capital-plan bridges; AEP/Duke docket queue; AEP Ohio tariff path; Duke Anderson County docket and approval release; Duke Carolinas Resource Plan filing.
what_this_proves: Regulated utility spend can be tracked through jurisdictional approval channels.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove every capital-plan dollar is approved, recoverable, or earning allowed returns.
next_required_evidence: Pull rate-case orders, CPCN orders, FERC Form 1, allowed ROE, CWIP/rider treatment, equity/debt financing plans, and final order conditions.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not treat parent-company capex as automatically rate-base approved.

claim: Load and reliability needs are becoming generation procurement, turbine reservations, acquisitions, and project approvals.
current_claim_grade: Level 4 for Duke Anderson; Level 3 for broader project table
strongest_current_evidence: Duke Anderson County PSCSC approval release and SC PSC docket; AEP I&M approved EGR path with pending 318 MW Big Sandy request; Duke 7,501 MW gas project table; secured turbines.
what_this_proves: Some generation capacity additions have named project or regulatory trails.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove full cost, return, financing stack, or in-service delivery.
next_required_evidence: Extract final orders, project costs, construction schedules, turbine contracts, ownership shares, financing treatment, and in-service milestones.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not treat planning-table MW the same as approved in-service MW.

claim: Infrastructure capital plans are pulling through to contractors, field crews, civil work, fiber, and building systems.
strongest_current_evidence: MasTec, Dycom, Primoris, and Granite backlog, book-to-bill, CAP, awards, miles, revenue, EBITDA/cash-flow evidence from power/grid extraction passes.
what_this_proves: Service-layer demand is visible and broad.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove backlog is funded, profitable, non-cancellable, or cash generative.
next_required_evidence: Extract backlog aging, funded-award status, customer concentration, gross margin, working capital, project reserves, claims, and owner capex links.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not treat backlog as profit or cash.

claim: Power, LNG, petrochemical, and industrial demand continue pulling capital into midstream logistics.
strongest_current_evidence: ONEOK and Targa capex, EBITDA, volumes, pipeline/logistics assets, project completions, liquidity, and debt evidence.
what_this_proves: Midstream remains a measurable capital-absorption lane.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not split growth from maintenance capex or prove project-level returns.
next_required_evidence: Extract project schedules, growth versus maintenance capex, contracted volumes, fee-based share, leverage, maturities, and project economics.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not call all midstream capex incremental growth.

claim: Refinancings and facilities are moving money through maturity relief, ABL changes, revolvers, and debt stack resets.
strongest_current_evidence: Refinancing event ledger pass 1 identifies 15 packet-derived rows across PBF, Liberty Broadband, Devon, Matador, Coterra, CNX, Ovintiv, Cenovus, Enhabit, and Wheaton, including ABL exit, senior-note refinancing, term-loan repayment, note redemption, convertible cleanup, facility amendment, and revolver/term-loan funding clues.
what_this_proves: The lane now has specific event rows, amounts, periods, instruments, and next-source requirements.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not yet prove full lender groups, coupons/spreads, collateral changes, extinguishment accounting, or post-close bank/private-credit roles.
next_required_evidence: Extract 10-K/10-Q/8-K debt tables, credit agreements, indentures, repayment language, maturity ladders, pricing, collateral, and use of proceeds for the named RFL rows.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not call refinancing growth funding unless use of proceeds supports it.

claim: M&A claims require financing proof before being treated as capital flowing into consolidation.
strongest_current_evidence: Acquisition finance ledger pass 1 identifies 12 rows across Core & Main, Verizon, Sherwin-Williams, Lowe's, Roblox, Expand Energy, Rio Tinto, Packaging Corporation of America, Silgan, and Phillips 66. Strongest packet-level row is PCA's 1.8B USD cash acquisition of Greif's containerboard business, adding two mills, about 800000 tons of capacity, and eight sheet feeder/corrugated plants.
what_this_proves: The lane now has named deal/context rows, visible asset/control consequences, and next-source requirements.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove lender groups, bridge loans, debt issued, assumed debt, cash/debt split, target debt repaid, or full purchase accounting across the lane.
next_required_evidence: Pull merger agreements, proxies, 8-Ks, acquisition notes, commitment letters, bridge loans, lender groups, assumed debt, debt issuance records, and purchase-accounting tables for the named AFL rows.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not equate transaction value with financing amount.

claim: Receivables, inventory, leases, and loans can turn operations into financeable collateral pools.
strongest_current_evidence: Asset-backed finance ledger pass 1 identifies 14 rows across Synchrony, Pool, Arrow, Global Industrial, MSC, Target, Dollar General, Zebra, Honeywell, and Henry Schein. Strongest filed rows are Synchrony's 102.2B USD Q2 2026 loan receivables and Pool's 315.5M USD Q2 2026 receivables-facility balance.
what_this_proves: The lane now has two true first-pass finance rows plus a broader collateral-search map for distributors, retailers, and equipment/healthcare middle layers.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove broad securitization, warehouse funding, collateral pledges, retained interests, advance rates, or trust-level loss performance across the lane.
next_required_evidence: Pull securitization notes, warehouse facilities, ABS prospectuses, receivables-facility agreements, credit-card trust data, receivables tables, advance rates, retained interests, and loss data for the named ABF rows.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not call working capital securitized unless a facility, note, sale, warehouse, pledge, or collateral transfer exists.

claim: The real economy is absorbing capital through capacity, throughput, industrial buildout, and infrastructure execution.
current_claim_grade: Level 3 source-table-backed plus first external denominator conversion funding-map credit-stack document-locator and filed-term-summary evidence
strongest_current_evidence: Capital-intensive buildout now has packet-ledger, project/cash queue, source-table rows, a project denominator workbench, a 14-row first-pass energy denominator extraction, a 16-row first-pass industrial denominator extraction, a 16-row first-pass industrial conversion extraction, a 20-row first-pass project funding map, a 20-row first-pass credit-agreement/project-finance extraction, a 16-row credit-document source-locator pass, and a 20-row filed-credit term-summary pass. United Rentals and Sterling add 22 Q2 2026 source-table rows plus 36 FY/Q4 2025 industrial annual-baseline rows. Energy Transfer and Cheniere add 24 Q2 2026 SEC-source rows plus 32 FY/Q4 2025 energy annual-baseline rows. ET has EIA denominators, cash/facility/debt capacity rows, revolver/commercial-paper/refinancing rows, identified January 2026 financing 8-K candidates, a 3.00B USD January 2026 coupon/maturity ladder, 1.60B USD of near-term redemptions, a 3.01x covenant-ratio clue, and 1.75B USD of July 2026 junior subordinated notes. Cheniere has DOE cargo rows, equity-funded growth-capex split rows, SPL/CQP/CCH/parent entity-debt rows, identified 2026 financing-event candidates, a 29.0B USD debt-and-interest schedule, and a 290.6B USD executed-SPA revenue denominator. URI has Census QSS/BEA/FRED denominators plus fleet-capex-to-cash, liquidity, ABL, AR securitization, term-loan, senior-note, identified facility-event candidate rows, 125.8% AR collateral coverage, and 37.0% ABL draw intensity. Sterling has Census/data-center denominator context plus backlog/cash, revolver-expansion, term-loan, credit-platform-reset, exact Exhibit 10.1 source-locator rows, a 450M USD pre-reset platform, a 1.5B USD July 2026 revolver, a 500M USD incremental base amount, and a 10 bp SOFR-adjustment elimination.
what_this_proves: The lane now has source-table support, first external physical/market-denominator support, first conversion support, first funding-map support, first credit-stack support, first document-locator support, and filed-term-summary support tying capital absorption to backlog, throughput, capacity investment, fleet spend, energy infrastructure, construction spending, machinery rental revenue, liquidity/debt context, operating cash generation, annual baselines, EIA export denominators, DOE LNG cargo rows, Census/FRED industrial denominators, URI fleet productivity/OEC/cash bridges, Sterling backlog/acquisition/cash bridges, company-level funding capacity, entity-level debt, secured/asset-backed facility evidence, agreement-document retrieval queue, coupons, maturities, covenant clues, collateral ratios, debt-service denominators, and credit-platform reset terms.
what_it_does_not_prove: It still does not fully distinguish growth, maintenance, inflation, compliance, replacement, acquisition capex, project returns, funded versus unfunded backlog, customer contract economics, ultimate source-of-funds, in-service status, train-specific production, terminal-specific utilization, fleet utilization by asset class, OEC mix, margins, debt-service waterfall, borrowing-base detail, covenant headroom, collateral eligibility, advance rates, use-of-proceeds by project, agreement terms, or organic versus acquired backlog conversion across all rows.
next_required_evidence: Extract full credit agreements, indentures, borrowing-base certificates, FERC LNG dockets, ET and Cheniere project finance tables, URI fleet utilization/OEC mix/rate/margin benchmarks and debt/facility tables, STRL customer/project sources, project-cost tables, customer/contract terms, debt-facility mapping, contract assets/liabilities, cargo-level reconciliation, use-of-proceeds, backlog roll-forwards, covenant calculations, collateral schedules, rating reports, repeated-period cash conversion, and actual agreement terms after compliant retrieval.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not treat source-backed capex, backlog, capacity, cargoes, contracts, OEC, DCF, EIA export denominators, DOE cargo counts, Census construction spending, QSS rental revenue, first-pass conversion ratios, company-level funding capacity, first-pass credit-stack evidence, document-locator rows, filed-term summaries, coupons, maturities, collateral ratios, or covenant clues as proof of project-level returns or ultimate source-of-funds until project/funding checks are extracted.

claim: Company-source claims must survive external denominator checks before becoming thesis-grade.
strongest_current_evidence: Outside-denominator plan for power/grid; bank denominator comparison; source hierarchy; all-company scale-up operating model; claim-status schema.
what_this_proves: The research has a clear method for moving from company numbers to external validation.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not mean every claim has completed denominator reconciliation.
next_required_evidence: Apply EIA, FERC, ISO, NAIC, FDIC, SEC ABS, rating-agency, state docket, and debt-market datasets to the highest-priority claims.
overclaim_to_avoid: Do not call the whole thesis proven because the method exists.
